title: Ace pride spade in cross-stitch
subtitle: A playing-card spade in the asexual pride flag colours on 14-count Aida
excerpt: An ace pride spade is a 55-by-65 stitch piece on 14-count Aida. A classic spade silhouette is filled with the four horizontal stripes of the asexual pride flag, black, grey, white, and purple, from top to bottom. Four floss colours. The ace-of-spades motif is a well-known symbol in asexual community spaces. Finished size is about 10 x 12 cm in a 12 cm hoop.
sourceNotes: Original design for Homemade cross-stitch library. The asexual pride flag was designed by AVEN in 2010. The ace-of-spades motif as an asexual symbol has been in community use since the early 2010s.

content.text: An ace pride spade is a 55-by-65 stitch piece on 14-count
. A classic spade silhouette, the pointed base, the two rounded lobes, and the narrow stem, is filled with the four horizontal stripes of the asexual pride flag. Four

colours (black, grey, white, purple) fill the shape in equal-depth bands. All full crosses. The stepped edges of the spade silhouette require careful chart-reading at the lobe curves, but no fractional stitches are needed.

items.name: 14-count Aida, white
items.substitutions: Pale grey Aida gives the white stripe a subtle definition

content.text: Find the fabric centre. The chart centre falls in the white stripe at the widest point of the spade. Begin there with blanc and work the stripe across its full width.
Work the grey stripe above the white (317), then the black band at the top of the lobes (310). Work the purple stripe below the white band (553) down to the base of the stem.
At the stepped lobe edges, follow the chart precisely, the lobes step outward by one stitch every two rows at the curve. Counting from the chart centre ensures both lobes stay symmetrical.
Wash gently and press face-down until the stitches sit smooth and flat. A small black or dark wood frame with no mount suits the monochrome-and-purple palette. Display in the hoop also works well.

items.cause: The left and right halves of the spade were stitched independently without checking against a shared centre axis.
items.fix: Mark the vertical centre of the spade on the chart and on the fabric before starting. Work both halves simultaneously, row by row, from the centre outward. Once each row is stitched on both sides, check that the stitch count is equal left and right.

items.symptom: The black areas look grey rather than solid
items.cause: Only two strands were used for the dark fill where three are needed, or the thread was not stripped before stitching.
items.fix: On 14-count Aida, two stripped strands should cover fully. If coverage looks thin, hold a test stitch up to the light: fabric squares should not be visible through the cross. If they are, add a strand. Once coverage is solid, continue with the corrected count throughout.

content.text: The trans flag heart uses the same stripe-fill approach in a different silhouette and a softer palette.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The default for beginners. Counted in squares per inch: 11ct, 14ct, 16ct, and 18ct are the common counts.

The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Each skein is made of six strands twisted together loosely; the stitcher strips out the number of strands needed for the fabric count (two strands for 14-count Aida) and threads them together.
